newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods fall with NYMEX, diffs mixed.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods fall with NYMEX, diffs mixed.

text.p: U.S. late spot refined products prices fell sharply by late Monday tracking February NYMEX futures, with differentials easing a bit in New York Harbor but tending to firm in the Gulf Coast, players said.

Spot activity was very thin Monday afternoon, with many brokers in Houston leaving their offices early to battle icy roads. A cold snap caused electrical outages that forced two links to the Colonial Pipeline to shut, although a pipeline spokesman said no reduction in line shipments occurred.
No refinery outages have been reported due to the cold blast, according to market watchers, since most of the plants are on the Gulf side of Houston, which was unaffected by ice.
U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded M4 gasoline diffs firmed about 0.15 cent, with offers for back 2nd cycle barrels on the Colonial Pipeline at 2.60 cents under NYMEX.
"There was a little spurt of action in the morning, but it really dried up later," one Gulf trader said.

New York Harbor "A5" grade reformulated gasoline saw diffs hold steady at about 0.30 cent below February futures, players said, with diffs on conventional unleaded easing a half cent to 2.50 cents below the print amid lackluster demand.
